correctness.rationale: On a strictly positive two-step orbit, the prey equations give y=λ−x−u/x, v=λ−u−x/u. Hence v−y=(x−u)(1−1/x−1/u), and x+u<2λ−2. For λ≤3 the reciprocal sum exceeds one by AM–GM, so unequal prey states force the opposite ordering of v−y to that required by h(x)h(u)=1 and nondecreasing h. Equal prey states force equal predator states, proving exclusion even at λ=3 without continuity. For each λ>3 one can choose z=2+(λ−3)/6, and x=z+ε,u=z−ε with both recovered predator states near Y=λ−z−1>0. Here v>y, so interpolating the reciprocal positive ratios v/y and y/v gives strictly positive slope. Its limiting intercept is 1−2(z−2)/Y in (0,1), as follows by writing the slope as (1−1/x−1/u)(v+y)/(vy). Sufficiently small positive ε preserves the strict inequalities and yields an exact period-two cycle. At r=1 the special h(x)=γx is still positive on x>0. The rational λ=4 witness was independently checked by exact substitution (both updates close); the supplied script was inspected, not run, and does not prove the universal threshold.
